data.label: Existing Git repository host
data.description: Existing repository with synthetic PR. Sends signed PR webhook; serves diff and file contents to a read-only, repo-scoped token. Never modified.

data.label: PR webhook endpoint
data.description: Receives PR events. A small validator checks the webhook signature and allowed repository, then enqueues. Rejects unknown repos.

data.label: Review job queue
data.description: Buffers review jobs keyed by repo+PR+head commit SHA for idempotent processing.

data.label: Failed review jobs
data.description: Holds jobs that failed repeatedly, for operator inspection.

data.label: PR review worker
data.description: Fetches only the authorized diff and relevant changed files (size-bounded), treats code as untrusted text and never executes it. Builds the prompt, calls the model, validates that each comment maps to a changed line, and stores drafts. No push or merge permissions.

data.label: Read-only repo credential
data.description: Stores the read-only repo token, readable only by the worker role. The value never appears in the diagram.

data.label: Review model
data.description: Foundation model invoked via Converse. Model ID, access, region and quotas still need verification. Mocked in local tests.

data.label: Draft review comments
data.description: Stores line-linked draft comments per PR/head SHA (file, line, side, text, model ID). Uses conditional writes for idempotency.

data.label: Human code reviewer
data.description: Reviews the drafts. Whether they get posted to the PR is an open decision.

data.label: Logs and metrics
data.description: Worker logs (no source code bodies), latency, errors and a DLQ depth alarm.

brief.application: Use AWS for this synthetic architecture qualification. Review a synthetic pull request from an existing repository. Retrieve only the authorized diff and relevant files, analyze it with AI, and draft review comments linked to changed lines. Preserve the existing repository. Never push, merge or execute repository code. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

lastAsked.question: What information will it work with, and where does it live?
lastAsked.beginner: For example a database, documents, or another system's data.
lastAsked.why: It shapes the AI architecture design.

requirements.statement: The system shall only read the authorized PR diff and relevant changed files. It shall never push, merge, check out or execute repository code.
requirements.rationale: Prevents changes to the repository and blocks code-execution or prompt-injection attacks through untrusted code.
requirements.basis: User: "Retrieve only the authorized diff and relevant files… Never push, merge or execute repository code."

requirements.statement: Every draft comment shall reference a file and a line that exists in the PR diff. Comments that can't be mapped to a changed line shall be rejected.
requirements.rationale: Comments on lines outside the diff mislead reviewers and can fail when posted.
requirements.basis: User: "draft review comments linked to changed lines"

requirements.statement: Proposed: model quality shall be checked against the real Bedrock model on a labelled set of synthetic PRs, kept separate from mocked local tests.
requirements.rationale: Mocked replies prove the plumbing works but say nothing about review quality, model access or quotas.
requirements.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation"

decisions.subject: design.aws-pr-review-assistant-first-end-to-end-sketch
decisions.title: AWS PR review assistant – first end-to-end sketch
decisions.context: Scope: review one synthetic PR from an existing repository: authorized diff retrieval, AI analysis, and line-linked draft comments. Read-only on the repository; no push, merge or code execution. Assumptions: the repo host supports signed webhooks and a read-only app token; Bedrock model and region not yet selected; whether comments get posted back is still undecided. The custom ingest and review components aren't covered by the native generator yet and still need engineering.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.
